sections.overview: This small Paraguayan cichlid belongs to the Gymnogeophagus mouthbrooder clade, which also includes Gymnogeophagus labiatus.
sections.identification: It has a relatively deep body, short caudal peduncle, and small overall size; adult males develop a lyre-shaped tail. The original description reports a maximum standard length of about 8.6 cm.
sections.habitat: It is known from the upper Tebicuary-mí River in Paraguay, using sandy patches among rocks in small streams and pools during low water.
sections.diet: Species-specific diet measurements were not reported in the sources consulted, so a detailed prey list cannot be given.
sections.behavior: The original account describes males quivering their mouths during courtship, a display associated with the genus’s mouthbrooding group.
sections.reproduction: It is a delayed maternal mouthbrooder: parents first lay eggs on a surface, then the female takes them into her mouth before hatching.
sections.ecology: At the type locality, it uses sandy bottoms among rocks in rivulets, with stronger currents in the rainy season and quieter pools in dry periods.
sections.conservation: The IUCN classifies it as Endangered because its very restricted range and habitat quality are declining under agricultural modification.
